# Verifying timed automata against branching real-time hyperproperties is undecidable

HCMTL extends metric temporal logic with quantifiers over executions that branch from previously chosen ones, to express security properties of real-time systems. Deciding whether a timed automaton satisfies an HCMTL sentence is undecidable in the interval-based semantics, already for the fragment HyperMITL; the source proves the same for a point-based semantics.

**Setting (Deka, Zhang, Chadha and Viswanathan).** Formulas of HCMTL (written HCMTL$^*$ in the source) are generated by

$$
\varphi ::= p_\pi \mid \neg p_\pi \mid \varphi \vee \varphi \mid \varphi \wedge \varphi \mid F_I\, \varphi \mid G_I\, \varphi \mid \varphi\, U_I\, \varphi \mid \exists \pi\, \varphi \mid \forall \pi\, \varphi,
$$

where $p$ is an atomic proposition, $\pi$ a path variable and $I$ an interval of nonnegative reals (singular intervals $[t, t]$ allowed); HyperMITL is the fragment in which all quantifiers occur at the front and intervals are non-singular. Systems are timed automata with state labels, clock invariants, guarded edges with resets and final states; executions are finite accepting runs, given as sequences of states with consecutive time intervals. In the interval-based semantics a formula is evaluated at a time $t$ under an assignment of executions to path variables; $\exists \pi\, \varphi$ holds if some accepting execution agreeing with the most recently quantified execution up to time $t$ (any execution at the start) satisfies $\varphi$ at $t$, dually for $\forall \pi$, and the temporal operators constrain times within $t + I$ as in MTL. The *general verification problem* asks, given a timed automaton and an HCMTL sentence, whether the automaton satisfies the sentence at time $0$. As an input to an algorithm, the clock constants of the automaton and the endpoints of the intervals of the sentence are rational numbers, or $\infty$ for a right endpoint; the source allows real endpoints in the logic.

**Theorem (Deka, Zhang, Chadha and Viswanathan).** The general verification problem for HCMTL is undecidable in the interval-based semantics, even for the fragment HyperMITL (Theorem 3, proved in Section V).

The source also proves undecidability, again for HyperMITL, in a point-based semantics, in which timed automata label events rather than states and formulas are evaluated at the event points of an execution (Theorem 16).

In contrast, the same paper proves that bounded-time verification, which considers only executions and times below a given bound, is decidable in both semantics.

## Expansion

As Ho and coauthors did for HyperMITL model checking, the universality problem for timed automata over finite timed words, which is undecidable, reduces to the general verification problem of HyperMITL in the point-based semantics. The paper shows that the point-based semantics reduces to the interval-based one, so the problem is undecidable there as well; for HCMTL with singular intervals, undecidability in the interval-based semantics also follows from the undecidability of verifying timed automata against MTL. A good expansion links pages for the undecidability of universality of timed automata over finite timed words, where executions are finite accepting runs (the result over infinite timed words with Büchi acceptance is a different problem), and for the reduction from the point-based to the interval-based semantics in Section V of the source.
